paper_sections.title: Structural MRI processing and MEG coregistration
MEG preprocessing, time-frequency transformation, and sensor-level statistics

description.value: The study examined age-related alterations in theta, alpha, and beta oscillatory dynamics during encoding, maintenance, and retrieval in a verbal working-memory task using MEG source imaging and whole-brain age correlations in healthy adults.

spans.text: In the current study, we investigated the neural mechanisms serving WM function in seventy-eight healthy aging adults (range: 20.2–65.2 years) using magnetoencephalography (MEG) and a Sternberg WM task with letter stimuli.

description.value: Observational healthy-aging study of HIV-negative adults across the adult lifespan; participants provided written informed consent and were studied during a modified Sternberg working-memory task.

spans.text: Modified Sternberg working memory paradigm.

description.value: Participants encoded and maintained six consonant letters presented in a 3 × 2 grid, followed by retrieval of a probe consonant and an in/out-of-set judgment.

spans.text: Participants were required to encode and maintain six letter stimuli. During the retrieval stage, participants were then required to indicate whether the probe letter was or was not present in the initial six letter set.
encoding phase

description.value: A six-consonant array was presented for 2.0 seconds for encoding.

spans.text: An array of six consonants then appeared at fixed locations within the grid for 2.0 s (i.e., encoding phase).
maintenance phase

description.value: The letters disappeared and the empty grid remained for 3.0 seconds while information was maintained.

spans.text: Following the encoding phase, the letters disappeared and the empty grid remained on the screen for 3.0 s (i.e., maintenance phase).
retrieval phase

description.value: A single probe consonant was presented for 0.9 seconds and participants judged whether it was in or out of the prior letter array.

spans.text: Finally, during the retrieval phase, a single probe consonant then appeared in the grid for 0.9 s, and the participant was instructed to respond via button press with their right index or middle finger as to whether the probe was in or out of the previous array of letters.

instructions.value: Respond via button press with the right index or middle finger as to whether the probe was in or out of the previous array of letters.

stimuli.value: Centrally presented fixation cross embedded in a 3 × 2 grid and arrays of six consonant letters, followed by a probe consonant.

spans.text: Participants were shown a centrally-presented fixation cross embedded in a 3 × 2 grid for 1.3 s ( Figure 1 ). An array of six consonants then appeared at fixed locations within the grid for 2.0 s (i.e., encoding phase).
